scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me start by understanding the situation.

So, there's this person who was renting a place with a roommate. When the lease was ending, the roommate just left without taking most of his stuff. He left a note saying he didn't want to bring some things with him. The landlord in this area has a policy where if you don't remove your stuff, they'll charge you to have someone do it, which can be expensive—like $250 taken from the deposit for just a few milk crates. That's pretty rip-off.

The person in question tried to contact the roommate for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or take it to the dump, but the roommate didn't respond. So, the person took most of the roommate's stuff to the dump. But there were also around 60 video games for the PS4. Instead of taking them to the dump, the person decided to sell them. They went to a local game store, sold all the games, and got $600.

Then, at a party, the roommate found out and got mad. The person explained that they tried to contact him but he didn't respond, so they sold the games. The roommate is now calling him an asshole and asking for the money back. Legally, there's nothing the roommate can do, but the person is wondering if they're the asshole for doing this.

Alright, so the question is: Is it morally acceptable for the person to sell the roommate's games without permission, given that the roommate didn't respond to their attempts to contact him?

First, I need to consider the moral principles involved here. Trust, responsibility, ownership, and fairness come to mind.

Ownership: The games belong to the roommate, right? So, selling them without permission would be taking someone else's property without consent. That's generally considered theft or at least a violation of property rights.

Responsibility: The person tried to contact the roommate to handle the stuff, but the roommate didn't respond. So, the person took it upon themselves to dispose of the stuff, including selling the games. Is that responsible? Or is it overstepping?

Trust: The roommate left the stuff, and the person took it upon themselves to sell it. That might break trust, especially if the roommate finds out and feels betrayed.

Fairness: The person got $600 from selling the games. Is it fair to keep that money, or should it go to the roommate? The roommate didn't respond, but the games are still his property.

But wait, the person was trying to avoid the landlord's rip-off fees. If they didn't dispose of the stuff, the landlord would have charged them, which could have cost more than $600. So, by selling the games, the person not only avoided that cost but also made some money. Is that justifiable?

Also, legally, there's nothing the roommate can do, but morally, is it acceptable? The person might argue that they were acting in their own interest to avoid financial loss, but they're using the roommate's property to do so.

Another angle: If the roommate didn't respond, maybe he didn't care about the stuff. So, by selling it, the person is making use of something the roommate didn't want. But still, ownership is a key factor here.

I'm also thinking about the concept of abandonment. If the roommate left the stuff and didn't respond, maybe he abandoned it. In some legal systems, abandonment can transfer ownership, but I'm not sure if that's the case here. The person checked legally and found nothing, so maybe it's not abandonment in this context.

So, putting it all together: The person sold the roommate's games without permission, which is a violation of ownership. Even though they tried to contact the roommate, and the roommate didn't respond, it's still not their property to sell. The fact that they made money from it and the roommate is upset adds to the moral issue.

Therefore, I think the action is morally unacceptable.
